newsitem.title: USA: Travelers sues Chris Craft, Zeneca units.
newsitem.headline: Travelers sues Chris Craft, Zeneca units.

text.p: A Travelers Group Inc subsidiary has sued Chris Craft Industries Inc and three units of Zeneca Group Inc for at least $14 million in damages for alleged fraudulent insurance claims.

In papers filed Thursday in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Travelers Indemnity Co said it paid the claims to Montrose Chemical Corp, which Travelers alleges is a "sham" company intended to insulate Chris Craft, Zeneca Holdings Inc, Zeneca Inc, and Stauffer Management Co from 10 pollution liability lawsuits filed against their predecessors since 1983.

In court papers, Travelers alleges the name of the defunct Montrose company was used to carry out "a scorched earth defense of the pollution liability actions solely to protect the billions of dollars in assets of the (real) joint venturers."

"As a result of the...fraudulent scheme to avoid liability, Travelers has paid twice to defend the interests of Stauffer Chemical, later Zeneca" and also paid benefits to Chris Craft even though it allegedly has no general liability insurance coverage with Travelers.

The pollution claims stem from a Torrance, California plant that made dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane, or DDT, an insecticide and environmental poison banned by the U.S. government for domestic use in 1972.

The plant was originally a joint venture of Stauffer Chemical Co and Montrose-Chemical Co of New Jersey, companies eventually succeeded by the Zeneca and Chris-Craft defendants. After 1982 the plant was closed, the equipment was sold and the site was paved over.
The lawsuits claim the DDT caused "harm to human health, harm to property, and damage to natural resources," court papers say.

Travelers said the plaintiffs sought to "insulate themselves from liability for the pollution...by creating the illusion that their defunct Montrose Chemical alter-ego is a separate and independent going concern."
Zeneca spokeswoman Judith Auchard said: "We can't comment until we've had a chance to study the papers." No one at Chris Craft could be reached for comment.
